senses.gloss: f. (b. h.) same, wickedness, guilt, indictable offense.
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 21a:20">Snh. 21ᵃ</cite> <he>איש חכם לר׳</he> ‘a wise man’ (<cite ref="II Samuel 13:3">II Sam. XIII, 3</cite>) wise for wickedness.

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 3:18">Koh. R. to III, 18</cite> <he>כל העובר … מדת רִשְׁעָתוֹ וכ׳</he> when one commits a sin shortly before his death, it is as if the measure of his wickedness wanted only this sin, and he completed it; a. fr.—Pl. (fr. <cite ref="T01105"><he>רִשְׁעוּת</he></cite>) <he>רִשְׁעִיּוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Ketubot 37a:8">Keth. 37ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 25:2">Deut. XXV, 2</cite>) <he>משום רשעה אחת … שתי ר׳</he> thou must punish him for one wrong, but not for two, i.e. not condemn him to corporal punishment and pecuniary restitution for the same act.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 7:1:2">Y. Ter. VII, beg. 44ᶜ</cite>; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 3:1:6">Y. Keth. III, 27ᵇ</cite> top <he>במי שיש בו שתי ר׳ וכ׳</he> the text (Deut. l. c.) speaks of one against whom there are two indictments (one criminal and one pecuniary).

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 105a:8">Snh. 105ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <he>רשעתים</he>, <cite ref="Judges 3:8">Jud. III, 8</cite>) <he>דעבד שתי ר׳ וכ׳</he> he did Israel two wrongs; Tanḥ. D’barim 3, v. <cite ref="T01098"><he>רָשַׁע</he></cite>; a. fr.—[<cite ref="Sanhedrin 112a:16">Snh. 112ᵃ</cite> <he>דרשעיות</he>, read: <he>דרַשְׁעָנִיּוֹת</he>.]
